sections.overview: Prosopocoilus astacoides is an Asian stag beetle with several named subspecies; its classification has been debated.
sections.identification: It belongs to Lucanidae, the stag beetle family. A taxonomic study found marked morphological and genetic differences among some populations assigned to its subspecies group.
sections.habitat: Published subspecies records span parts of South and Southeast Asia, including northeastern India, Myanmar, Java and Sumatra; these do not describe one uniform range for every population.
sections.diet: The sources consulted here do not establish a species-specific wild diet.
sections.behavior: Wild behavior is poorly documented in the sources consulted; captive observations should not be treated as a full account of its natural history.
sections.reproduction: Captive breeding research on the subspecies blanchardi measured mating and egg-laying, but those conditions do not establish the timing of reproduction in wild populations.
sections.ecology: Some forms once treated within P. astacoides have been raised to species rank, while genetic work has questioned the boundaries of others; subspecies names therefore require care.
sections.conservation: A Korean study describes the subspecies blanchardi as endangered; that assessment should not be generalized to the whole species.
